title: Escalated-tenant fastpath + surge suppression for Hosted API 5xx/timeouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Customer reports repeated 5xx and upstream timeouts during a region-wide tenant surge. This ticket implements a low-risk, high-priority mitigation: a temporary "fastpath" routing rule for escalated tenants that bypasses nonessential proxy stages and applies a soft-suppression policy for automated retries to avoid amplification. Work includes runtime routing change, circuit-breaker tuning, telemetry augmentation, canary rollout plan, and runbook updates for SRE/CS during active escalations.
impact_summary: A subset of customers experienced cascaded 5xx responses and amplified retries when an increased request pattern caused KV-cache thrashing and proxy queue saturation. This fix reduces end-to-end latency for designated escalated tenants and prevents retry storms that worsen host degradation. Expected to reduce customer-visible 5xx by ~70% for targeted tenants during surges.
reproducer: Load test: 200 concurrent streams per tenant with 30% long-sequence (3k tokens) requests while toggling client retry SDK default (3 retries). Observed proxy queue growth, increased p99 latency, and 502/504s originating from runtime task timeouts.
steps_taken: Validated incident traces in console: tenant-scoped traces show proxy queue hold times and repeated backend calls from SDK retries
Created temporary feature-flagged routing rule (ff=escalation_fastpath_v1) to short-circuit nonessential middleware for test tenants
Instrumented additional tags: tenant_escalation=true, retry_suppressed=true for telemetry correlation
Deployed circuit-breaker tweak (downstream timeout floor + dynamic max-inflight per-tenant) to staging and ran synthetic with reproduction harness
Prepared a rollback plan and traffic-shaping knobs for rapid mitigation

decisions: Implement FF-gated fastpath routing rather than immediate global config change to limit blast radius
Suppress automated SDK retries for escalated tenants by returning Retry-After + 429 where safe instead of propagating 502/504s to cause amplification
Avoid deep changes to KV cache eviction algorithm in this patch to minimize regression risk; schedule as follow-up for runtime team
Add tenant-scoped dynamic max-inflight configuration rather than static global limits to preserve latency SLOs for healthy tenants
